projects.title: Smart Contact Lens for Intraocular Pressure Monitoring
paragraphs: This AMED-supported research focuses on real-time intraocular pressure monitoring using smart contact lenses.

The system integrates flexible PEDOT-based resistive sensors and wrinkled-gold capacitive sensors with parity–time (PT)-symmetric wireless readout. Antenna design and electromagnetic simulation were performed using HFSS, while sensor and wireless performance were evaluated through VNA and LCR measurements.
The sensors were integrated into hydrogel contact lenses in collaboration with Vizionfocus, followed by experimental validation using ex vivo porcine eyes and in vivo rabbit eyes.
The research led to publications in npj Flexible Electronics and ACS Sensors and an accepted paper in Advanced Materials Technologies. Waseda University also featured the research.

projects.title: Wireless Smart Contact Lens for Eye-Movement Recognition
paragraphs: My current research explores wireless smart contact lenses for eye-movement recognition using flexible sensors.
We fabricate flexible sensors and microscale devices, then measure their electrical and wireless responses. The measurements guide the design of the sensing system.

projects.title: Flexible Antenna and Wireless Power Transfer
paragraphs: For my master’s research, we fabricated flexible wrinkled-gold antennas and chemically bonded them to commercial soft contact lenses. The aim was to deliver power wirelessly to electronics on the lens.
Wireless power transfer was demonstrated by illuminating an LED integrated into the contact lens.
